name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+10 partisan lean favors the Democratic incumbent
Peters holds a roughly $2.6M cash edge while Cohen reports no fundraising

model.rationale: The seat's ten-point Democratic lean, Peters' overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing his win near 96% all point the same way, with no contrary polling or expert ratings to suggest a closer contest. Cohen's lack of any reported fundraising leaves little evidence of a competitive campaign.
model.watch: Any public polling showing a single-digit race, a late surge of outside spending for Cohen, or a sharp national shift toward Republicans would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He enters the general election with roughly $2.6 million on hand after raising $1.8 million, while Republican Steve Cohen reports no fundraising totals, leaving Peters with a decisive resource edge. Prediction markets put Peters' chances near 96 percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, Peters' incumbency, and the money gap. All three point in the same direction, and the seat has consistently favored Democrats in recent cycles. Cohen would need a dramatic shift in the national environment or a late influx of outside spending to put the race in play, and there is no current sign of either.
